_note: WhatsDaf's own English renderings of the Hebrew commentaries on Sefaria (Vilna edition). Keys are <commentary>:<amud><segment>.<comment>. Square brackets are our clarifications. Very long Tosafot are condensed and marked "In brief".
rashi:a1.1: Gemara. “He [hu]”: we expound it as “keep him alive [haḥayehu],” for this is its sense: he shall remain alive from your valuation.
gershom:a1.1: Sustain him from your valuation: that is, give him his living out of your valuation.
gershom:a2.1: And the Rabbis, who did not speak either of the pair of oxen or of the donkey: they hold that these are property, and one does not give them to him.
rashi:a5.1: Until now, when he had an extra adze to lend, they would lend him saws.
gershom:a3.1: Until now: when he had many adzes, he could lend, and from the one to whom he lent an adze he would borrow a saw in its place, and so he had all the saws he needed. Now that he has only two adzes, so that there is nothing to lend, [one might think] one should give him more of the type he has few of, or leave him three of the type he has many of. It teaches us that this is not so.
rashi:a6.1: Remove his phylacteries: take his phylacteries off his head, until he redeems them for money.
rashi:a7.1: I am performing a mitzva: in that I am giving to Temple maintenance. Therefore his intention was for all his property.
rashi:a8.1: Mishna. He has no [right] to his wife’s garment: since it is not his.
gershom:a4.1: He has no [right]: that is, the treasurer has no right to take.
rashi:a8.2: For their sake: for the sake of his wife and his children.
rashi:a8.3: New sandals: it teaches us a novelty: even though they have not yet worn them, they retain their status [as theirs] from the time of purchase.
gershom:a5.1: Not the garment of his wife and children: even though they have not yet worn them.
rashi:a9.1: Although they said slaves are sold in their garments for profit: for their fine garment improves them and raises their price, as in the case of orphans’ property: if a garment of thirty dinars is bought for the slave, it improves him by a maneh over the price he is worth now.
gershom:a6.1: Although they said slaves are sold in their garments for profit: for their garments improve them and they are sold dearly.
gershom:a7.1: And likewise a cow: is sold [dearly].
rashi:a9.3: To the city: where merchants usually come.
gershom:a9.1: And likewise a pearl, if they take it up to the city it appreciates: none of these are moved from their place to bring them to where prices are high. Rather, they are reckoned as they are worth in the place of the one who consecrates or valuates, and at the time that he consecrates it. This is: “It has only its location and its time.”
rashi:a9.4: The Temple treasury has only its location: this refers to the pearl.
rashi:a9.5: And its time: this refers to the slave and the cow. For one who valuates himself and is poor is judged by affordability, and gives the Temple according to what he has. If he had a slave who is appraised now at twenty zuz, one does not say: we view it as though a garment were bought for him for thirty zuz, and it improves him by a maneh, so that he would be sold for a hundred and twenty zuz, and the slave’s price comes to ninety zuz, and so this one must give the Temple. Rather, he is appraised according to his time. And likewise the cow; and likewise a pearl in a village is appraised only according to its location.
tosafot:a9.1: The Temple treasury has only its location and its time. And if you say: if so, why must the appraisal of consecrated property wait sixty days [of proclamation]? In all these cases here one does not wait, even though waiting would be to the Temple’s gain. And one cannot say that here we are speaking of one who consecrated all his property, and that is why proclamation does not apply; that is not so, for it is taught in the Tosefta of our chapter that even if he consecrated only a pearl by itself, the law is the same, that one does not wait. One can say: here we are speaking of movable property, and it is stated in the chapter Almana Nizonet (Ketubot 100b) that one does not proclaim these, lest they be stolen; whereas the first clause of the mishna [of this chapter], which requires proclamation for sixty days, speaks of land.
rashi:a10.1: Gemara. That he should not delay a pearl for the light ones: for a light and poor person who valuated himself and has a pearl, the treasurer should not hold it back from him, saying: Take it up to the city and give according to that price. Rather, it is appraised according to what it is worth here; and this one holds on to it and sells it for whatever he wishes, and gives according to the price at which they appraised it, since at the time the priest valuated him he had no more.
gershom:a10.1: “As of that day”: that he should not delay a pearl for the light ones. That is, if he valuated himself and he is a light and poor person, and he has a pearl that is worth, in his hand and in his place, only a shekel, it is reckoned at a shekel, and he is judged by affordability and is exempt. And one does not say: let them hold it until it is sold dearly, and he will not be judged by affordability. The verse teaches: “on that day.”
gershom:a11.1: Unspecified consecration is for Temple maintenance: a place where it comes wholly to the Lord, for the building, and no benefit from it goes either to the priests or to the altar.
rashi:a12.1: Mishna. One may not consecrate an ancestral field less than two years before the Jubilee: for it is written of one who consecrates an ancestral field, “according to the years that remain” (Leviticus 27:18), and “years” are no fewer than two.
tosafot:a12.1: One may not consecrate, etc. [Only the heading is printed here.]
gershom:a13.1: One may not consecrate: [a field, the sowing-area of a ḥomer of barley].
rashi:a12.2: Nor may one redeem less than one year after the Jubilee: it is explained in the Gemara, Rav according to his reasoning and Shmuel according to his.
gershom:a15.1: [Nor may one redeem after the Jubilee: this “after the Jubilee” the Gemara explains as speaking of all the years of the Jubilee cycle.
gershom:a16.1: Less than a year: if he comes to redeem it ten and a half years after the Jubilee, he may not say: Since the year is not complete, I will not give a sela and a pundeyon for it. Rather, it is counted as a full year, and he gives a sela and a pundeyon for it along with the remaining years. This is: “Nor may one redeem for less than a year.”]
rashi:a12.3: And one does not count, etc.: it is explained in the Gemara.
rashi:a12.4: But the Temple treasury counts months: that is, if it is to the Temple’s gain, we count the half year that has passed as having passed. As is explained below: where he consecrated it in the middle of the forty-eighth year, if you count that half year as passed, it is less than two years before the Jubilee, and it is redeemed not with a deduction but for fifty; and if you do not count those months that have passed, it is two years before the Jubilee, and there is a loss to the Temple, which takes only two sela and two pundeyon. Here, certainly, they count it as fully passed.
rashi:a13.1: Gemara. And they raised a contradiction: “One may consecrate both before the Jubilee”: which implies even less than two years before it.
gershom:a17.1: It initially occurs to [the Gemara] that “one may not consecrate” less than two years before the Jubilee means not at all, that is, the field is not consecrated. And they raised a contradiction: One may consecrate before the Jubilee, etc. [and] after the Jubilee: even right next to the Jubilee itself.
rashi:a14.1: Rav and Shmuel both say: one may not consecrate to be redeemed with a deduction less than two years. One who consecrates an ancestral field in the first year of the Jubilee cycle and comes to redeem it gives fifty sela per beit kor, as it is written: “The sowing of a ḥomer of barley [at fifty shekels of silver]” (Leviticus 27:16). And if he consecrated it ten or twenty years after the Jubilee, one counts the years remaining until the next Jubilee, and he gives a sela and a pundeyon for each year, as it is written: “But if he sanctifies his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall reckon for him [the money according to the years that remain] … and a deduction shall be made from your valuation” (Leviticus 27:18). This is the deduction: that he does not give fifty sela. And one who consecrates two years before the Jubilee redeems it for two sela and two pundeyon, as it is written: “according to the years that remain.” And so the calculation for redeeming an ancestral field comes to a sela and a pundeyon for each year: for if he consecrated it in the first year after the Jubilee, he would redeem it for fifty shekels, as it is written: “If he sanctifies his field from the Jubilee Year” (Leviticus 27:17), “from the year,” and the Jubilee Year is not included. Evidently the verse speaks of the year after the Jubilee, and it says he gives fifty. Set aside forty-nine sela for the forty-nine coming years until the next Jubilee, and one sela remains beyond the sela for each year. Divide it into pundeyonin, for a sela has forty-eight pundeyonin: that makes a sela and a pundeyon for each year, less one pundeyon. Therefore one who consecrates his field two or three years after the Jubilee gives a sela and a pundeyon for each year until the Jubilee. And although, when you count a sela and a pundeyon for forty-nine years, you find fifty sela and a pundeyon, that is, forty-nine sela and forty-nine pundeyonin, while the sela is only forty-eight pundeyonin, we already raised this in Bekhorot, in the chapter Yesh Bekhor LeNaḥala (50a): What is the nature of this pundeyon? It is an exchange fee [kolbon] for the small change. And Rav and Shmuel say that one who consecrates less than two years before the Jubilee has no law of deduction here, and if he comes to redeem it he gives fifty sela, for regarding the deduction it is written: “according to the years that remain … and a deduction shall be made,” and the minimum of “years” is two. And our mishna teaches us good advice: that a person should be concerned about his property and not redeem [so the printed Rashi; the Gemara says “consecrate”] less than two years before the Jubilee, so that he does not lose forty-eight sela.
tosafot:a14.1: In brief: Rav and Shmuel mean one may not consecrate to redeem for less than two sela and two pundeyon. For whenever he or another redeems it during the years of the Jubilee cycle, in the twentieth or the thirtieth, it is redeemed by the years remaining until the Jubilee, a sela and a pundeyon a year: forty-nine sela for forty-nine years leaves a sela, which is forty-eight pundeyon, and that is the pundeyon brought as an exchange fee [kolbon], as in Bekhorot (50a). But if he redeems less than two years before the Jubilee he deducts nothing and redeems the sowing-area of a kor for fifty full sela, as it is written: “according to the years that remain until the Jubilee Year, and a deduction shall be made from your valuation” (Leviticus 27:18), and the minimum of “years” is two. So the tanna teaches that a person should be concerned about his property and not consecrate less than two years before the Jubilee. Question: then let it also teach that one should not consecrate in the first year of the Jubilee cycle, since then too he redeems without a deduction. First answer: that was unnecessary, since the one who consecrates knows that he will redeem without a deduction and has accepted it, for it is fifty sela for forty-nine years, at the rate of a sela and a pundeyon a year; here, however, little remains until the Jubilee, so the tanna had to tell him to be concerned. Second answer: it does not say so of the first year because he can wait until three years before the Jubilee and then give only three sela and three pundeyon; so the tanna warned only about less than two years, when he must give fifty full sela, and if he waits until the Jubilee the field will not return to him again. Question: what does the mishna teach us, given the baraita that one may consecrate both before and after the Jubilee? Answer [the text here is difficult]: although the year begins at Rosh HaShana, the Jubilee does not begin until Yom Kippur; “after the Jubilee” means after the Rosh HaShana that ends the Jubilee Year, and we do not say the Jubilee Year runs until Yom Kippur. Open on Sefaria for the full text.
gershom:a14.1: Less than two years before the Jubilee: for if he consecrated it, he pays fifty shekels [as is explained in the Gemara], for it teaches us good advice, that a person should be concerned about his property. One who consecrates his field two years before the Jubilee and afterward redeems it, [pays] according to the years from the redemption until the Jubilee: for those years that it is in the Temple’s possession he deducts [i.e., reckons] for the Temple a sela and a pundeyon for each year, and gives the Temple a sela and a pundeyon a year per kor, and it is his. For so the calculation of fifty shekels comes out: forty-nine shekels for the forty-nine years of the Jubilee, while the fiftieth year is not counted, since it counts for both cycles; the remaining shekel he divides into pundeyonin, and a shekel has forty-eight pundeyon, and he deducts a sela and a pundeyon for each year except one year. And although one year lacks a pundeyon, since if one sought to divide it evenly over all the years it would come to less than a pundeyon a year, and he wanted to count only a whole coin, therefore it says a sela and a pundeyon. And for all those years of the Jubilee cycle that the field was his before he consecrated it, he gives nothing. But if he consecrated it less than two years before the Jubilee and comes to redeem it, he does not give two sela and two pundeyon for those two years and no more; rather, he pays fifty shekels for a ḥomer of barley. [A printer’s note says the verse quoted here is not written in this passage at all, and it should read: as it is written:] “Then the priest shall reckon for him the money according to the years that remain until the Jubilee Year, and a deduction shall be made from your valuation.” “If there are yet many years, according to them he shall return his redemption” [Leviticus 25:51]: that is, if when he consecrated it at least two years still remained, he returns his redemption according to them, a sela and a pundeyon a year per kor. And if he consecrated it less than two years before the Jubilee, so that two years did not remain, he gives the whole fifty shekels.
gershom:a18.1: And in the Jubilee Year itself one may not consecrate: the reason is explained below.] Rav and Shmuel seek to resolve the mishna: what is “one may not consecrate”? It does not teach that one may not consecrate at all; rather, one may not consecrate with the intention that he can redeem with a deduction, as it is written [a printer’s note: here too there is an error, and it should read]: “Then the priest shall reckon for him according to the years that remain,” that is, that he deducts, etc. “And if few remain of the years until the Jubilee Year, he shall reckon with him; according to his years he shall return his redemption” [Leviticus 25:52]: that is, that he deducts from the redemption and gives only a sela and a pundeyon for each year that belonged to the Temple. Hence, if he consecrated it less than two years before the Jubilee, he does not redeem it [with a deduction] but for the whole fifty shekels together. And since [one may not consecrate to be redeemed with a deduction less than two years], our mishna teaches us good advice, that one should be concerned about his property and not consecrate at a time when he cannot redeem with a deduction. That is why it says “one may not consecrate, etc.”: so that he not lose, and not that sanctity does not take effect on the field.
gershom:a19.1: Rav said it is consecrated: and if he comes to redeem it, he gives the whole fifty shekels.
rashi:a16.1: Granted, with regard to sale: regarding one who sells his field in the Jubilee Year itself, Shmuel disagrees with Rav below, in the chapter HaMokher (Arakhin 29b), because one can say an a fortiori inference.
gershom:a20.1: [Granted, with regard to sale: regarding one who sells his field in the Jubilee Year, Shmuel disagrees with Rav below, holding that it is not sold, because one can say an a fortiori inference: if a field sold before the Jubilee now leaves and returns to the owner, is it not logical that one not sold now, in the Jubilee Year, cannot be sold at all in the Jubilee Year? But here, can one say an a fortiori inference: if a consecrated field already leaves to the owner at the Jubilee, is it not logical that sanctity cannot take effect at all on one not consecrated now, in the Jubilee Year?]
rashi:a17.1: Can one say an a fortiori inference? Those consecrated fields already do not leave the Temple’s possession at the Jubilee without redemption, for we learned (below, Arakhin 25b): If the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed, the priests enter into it and give its value to the Temple, for Temple maintenance.
gershom:a21.1: But didn’t we learn: that it does not return to the owner.
gershom:a22.1: Rather, if the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed, the priests enter into it and give its value to the Temple; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. Evidently it belongs to the Temple; so too it should become consecrated at the time of the Jubilee.
rashi:a18.1: Holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon: therefore one can say the a fortiori inference: if a field already consecrated leaves now, is it not logical that one not consecrated cannot become consecrated?
gershom:a23.1: No: Shmuel holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who said they enter into it and do not give its value to the Temple; rather, it is theirs. And just as its value does not go to the Temple, so too it is not consecrated when he consecrated it in the Jubilee Year.
rashi:b1.1: And Rav says to you: according to Rabbi Shimon this is not a leaving [from the Temple], for ultimately, does it return to the owner?
tosafot:b1.1: Ultimately, does it return to the owner? And if you say: why does he need to answer this way? Let him simply say that he does not accept Shmuel’s a fortiori inference. One can say: because below (Arakhin 29b), regarding the dispute of Rav and Shmuel about one who sells his field in the Jubilee Year itself, it says: What is Shmuel’s reason? An a fortiori inference: if a field already sold, etc. And it objects there: And does Rav not state an a fortiori inference of this kind? But it is taught: Might one sell his daughter when she is a young woman? You said, it is an a fortiori inference, etc. And it answers there: there, she does not return and get sold again; here, it returns and gets sold again. Evidently they accept it. Were it not for this explanation, Rav too would have had to derive the a fortiori inference, as we derive it regarding one who sells his daughter as a young woman. Therefore Rav needed here to refute the a fortiori inference, and this is the meaning: ultimately, does it return to the owner? And since it no longer returns to the owner, it is no longer consecrated by the law of an ancestral field.
gershom:b1.1: And Rav says: ultimately, even according to Rabbi Shimon, does it return to the owner? It is to the priests that it goes out, and one can still say that it is consecrated property; and in any case they do not give its value, because the priests receive from the table of the Most High. (A printer’s note follows, saying that Shmuel’s reason can still well be explained as following Rabbi Shimon; its wording is unclear.)
gershom:b2.1: What is Rav’s reason: who said that it is consecrated.
tosafot:b2.1: In brief: Question: why does the Gemara need to give Rav’s reason from the verse, once he has refuted the a fortiori inference, since Shmuel’s main reason is the a fortiori inference? Answer: Rav perforce had to say that “if from the Jubilee Year” means the Jubilee Year is included, as Rabbi holds at the beginning of the chapter HaSeg Yad (18b), “the first, and the first is included.” For if “from the Jubilee Year” meant the year after the Jubilee, as Shmuel says, then since the verse did not speak of the Jubilee Year itself, we would say that if one consecrated in it, it is redeemed at its market value and not in the order of the other years, by the reckoning of the sowing of a ḥomer of barley at fifty shekels of silver. So it is explained in the Tosafot, though this is somewhat difficult below. My teacher the RaMaR explained instead: since the verse did not speak of the Jubilee Year itself, we would say it is not consecrated at all, as Shmuel says; therefore the Gemara had to explain that Rav holds like Rabbi, that “from the Jubilee Year” includes the Jubilee Year. Question: if Rav holds the verse includes the Jubilee Year, why did he need to refute the a fortiori inference, since the verse explicitly includes it? Answer: if the a fortiori inference were sound, even Rabbi would not say that “from the Jubilee Year” includes it; we would say, even according to Rabbi, by the force of the a fortiori inference, that it means the year after the Jubilee, as Shmuel says. Accordingly it is also fine to say that even Shmuel speaks according to Rabbi in saying it is not consecrated, since the a fortiori inference shows that here the Jubilee Year is not included. That is why Rav Yosef had to explain Shmuel’s reason by the a fortiori inference, for it cannot be that the dispute of Rav and Shmuel is simply a dispute of tannaim; rather, they certainly disagree according to Rabbi, as their reasons were explained. But according to the Rabbis, even Rav agrees that one who consecrates in the Jubilee Year itself, it is not consecrated, as is stated below in our passage. Open on Sefaria for the full text.
rashi:b4.1: Granted, according to Rav, this is what is written: “If from the Jubilee Year”: fifty sela; “if after the Jubilee”: a deduction.
rashi:b4.2: But according to Shmuel, what is “after the Jubilee”? The first verse, which requires fifty, also speaks of after the Jubilee.
gershom:b3.1: [The verse states, etc. But according to Shmuel, what is “after the Jubilee”?]
rashi:b4.3: After the after: for example, two or three years after the Jubilee there is a deduction; but if he consecrated it in the year right after the Jubilee there is no deduction.
gershom:b4.1: After the after: that is, “if from the Jubilee Year” means from the year after the Jubilee and not the Jubilee itself, and “if after” means the after of the after, that is, the third year.
rashi:b5.1: It is not consecrated to be redeemed with a deduction: since there is a full Jubilee cycle here.
rashi:b6.1: By inference: that what it teaches in that baraita, “one may consecrate before the Jubilee,” means to be redeemed with a deduction. But Rav and Shmuel, etc.
rashi:b7.1: Rav says to you: certainly, what it teaches, “one may consecrate,” certainly means to give fifty, and in the Jubilee Year it is not consecrated at all. And this is no difficulty for me, for whose is this? It is the Rabbis’, who disagree with Rabbi in the chapter HaSeg Yad (above, Arakhin 18b) and say: “the first,” and the first is not included.
tosafot:b7.1: Rav could say to you: whose is this? It is the Rabbis’, and I spoke according to Rabbi. According to the explanation of the Tosafot, who explained above that since the verse did not speak of the Jubilee Year itself, we would have said that if one consecrated in it, it is consecrated to be redeemed at its value, how can the Rabbis say that in the Jubilee Year itself one may not consecrate, and if he consecrated it is not consecrated? We should have said that if he consecrated in it, it is consecrated, to be redeemed at its value. But according to the explanation of my teacher the RaMaR it is fine.
gershom:b5.1: [Rav could say to you: whose is this, that teaches “in the Jubilee Year itself one may not consecrate”?
gershom:b6.1: It is the Rabbis’, who do not hold “until, and the until is included,” and expound “from the year,” and not the actual year.
rashi:b7.2: And I said it in accordance with Rabbi: but according to Shmuel, even according to Rabbi it is not consecrated. For when Rabbi says “from the first day,” and the first is included, that is there, where “until” is written, so that the expression “from the day” fits; but here, where “until” is not written, it would have had to write “in the year,” and so Rabbi concedes that it is not included.
gershom:b7.1: And I said it in accordance with Rabbi: who holds “until, and the until is included,” as he said: “from the first day until the seventh day,” the first, and the first, etc.
rashi:b8.1: If Rabbi expounds here “from the year,” and the year is included, evidently the verse speaks of the Jubilee Year and says he gives fifty sela. What is the purpose of the pundeyon? When one consecrates ten or twenty years before the Jubilee, why [does he give a sela and a pundeyon]? Let him give a sela a year. For since one who consecrates and redeems it in the Jubilee Year itself gives only fifty, it turns out that each year of the cycle comes to only a sela, since from here until the next Jubilee is fifty years, this year included. Therefore, when he redeems it two or three years before the Jubilee, he should need to give only a sela for each year, and no more.
tosafot:b8.1: If like Rabbi, what is the purpose of the pundeyon? And if you say: why does it need to object on the grounds that he holds like Rabbi? It should have objected to Rav directly from what we learned (below, Arakhin 25a): If he consecrated it two or three years before the Jubilee, he gives a sela and a pundeyon a year; and if the Jubilee Year itself is consecrated like the other years of the cycle, what is the purpose of the pundeyon? One can say: from that mishna he could have answered that it is the Rabbis’, as he answered above; but from Rabbi it objects well, for Rabbi says so, as the Talmud explains.
gershom:b8.1: If like Rabbi, what is the purpose of the pundeyon? That is, since he counts the fiftieth year in the reckoning of the Jubilee years together with the forty-nine, for it too becomes consecrated in the Jubilee Year, if so, the fiftieth shekel, why does one divide it so that there is a pundeyon for each year? Since the fiftieth year is consecrated like the other years of the cycle, let him give the fiftieth shekel for that year itself.
gershom:b9.1: And if you say: indeed he does not hold a pundeyon a year; but it is taught: If he consecrated it two, etc.
rashi:b9.1: Counts for both: the Jubilee Year belongs to the Jubilee that has passed, and one counts it as one year toward the next Jubilee. Therefore, with this year, there are only forty-nine until the next Jubilee Year, and the next Jubilee Year is not counted with them, since the Jubilee releases at its beginning, and once the Jubilee Year begins, if another person redeemed it, it goes out to the priests, as it is written: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee” (Leviticus 27:21). It turns out that one who redeems an ancestral field in the Jubilee Year itself, when it was consecrated, has it in his hand only forty-nine years, and he gives fifty sela, which comes to a sela and a pundeyon for each year.
gershom:b10.1: Rabbi, who holds a pundeyon a year, holds like Rabbi Yehuda, who said:] The fiftieth year counts for both. And since he counts it also as the start of the Jubilee years, he does not count a shekel for it itself, but divides it into pundeyonin.
rashi:b10.1: According to Shmuel: who says that here Rabbi concedes that it is “from the year,” and the year is not included, and the verse speaks of the year after the Jubilee and says that he gives fifty.
rashi:b10.2: Let him say that Rabbi, who says he gives a sela and a pundeyon a year,
rashi:b10.3: holds like the Rabbis: who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda, that the year of the Jubilee that passed is not part of the count of the next Jubilee, and apart from that year there are forty-nine years here. For if he held like Rabbi Yehuda, who says the cycle has only forty-eight years apart from the year of the Jubilee that passed, and the verse speaks of the year after the Jubilee, it would turn out that he gives fifty sela for forty-eight years, which comes to a sela and two pundeyon.
gershom:b11.1: According to Shmuel, who said it is not consecrated, [let him say] that Rabbi, who holds a pundeyon a year, holds like the Rabbis, who do not hold that the fiftieth year counts for both; rather, it stands by itself for the Jubilee. Therefore he divides its own shekel into pundeyonin, according to Shmuel, who said it is not consecrated.
gershom:b12.1: For if he held like Rabbi Yehuda, that it counts for both, for the start of the count of forty-nine and as the fiftieth year, there would be only forty-eight years from Jubilee to Jubilee; two shekels would remain, divide them into pundeyonin, and it would come out that for each year [he should require] a sela and two pundeyon.
gershom:b13.1: Perforce, according to Shmuel [who said it is not consecrated], he holds like the Rabbis, who count the fiftieth year only at the end of the cycle; and since he said it is not consecrated, its shekel is left over, and he divides it into pundeyonin, and it comes to only a sela and a pundeyon a year.
rashi:b11.1: Granted, according to Shmuel, less than a year: it says that our mishna teaches us that if he consecrated it in the Jubilee Year itself, it need not be redeemed, since it was not consecrated.
gershom:b14.1: Granted, according to Shmuel, who said it is not consecrated: that is what is taught, “one may not redeem and not consecrate after the Jubilee less than a year,” to exclude the Jubilee Year itself, in which one neither consecrates nor redeems.
gershom:b15.1: But according to Rav, [who said] that it is consecrated, what is “after the Jubilee”?
gershom:b16.1: [Rav could say to you:] Do you hold that “after the Jubilee” is the actual after-Jubilee, the year next to the Jubilee, so that you infer from it to exclude the Jubilee itself? No.
gershom:b17.1: [What is “after the Jubilee”? In the middle of the Jubilee cycle, that is, in all the years after the Jubilee.]
